North star: what this dashboard is for

Read this before any refresh or new feature. A change that doesn't help answer one of the questions below can wait.

The goals

  1. Investing. The clearest risk-adjusted long and short ideas across about 400 small and mid-cap biotechs, built the same way every month and scored against later prices, so the record is real and keeps improving.
  2. Buy-side healthcare ECM (Balyasny, Citadel). Know who will raise before the call comes: roughly how much, when, and whether we take part, pass or short into the deal.
  3. Gaps. Areas with many patients but no strong public drug, crowded areas where the weaker players get consolidated, and companies trading below cash.

One line: a disciplined, scored biotech process that makes better long/short calls and sees supply coming before the Street does.

The three questions we must answer best

The Brief page opens with a panel that answers all three from live data; each answer links to the page behind it.

  1. What kind of stocks did best and worst, in which periods, and what did we learn? → Brief panel (consistent winners and losers, the lesson, next quarter's call) and Record › What worked, 2025–2026: each stock grouped as it stood at the start of each quarter, 1/2/4-quarter holds, best and worst group per quarter, top 5 examples plus an exception each way, and a written call for next quarter (data/backdrop.json).
  2. What are our top longs and shorts, and what do we see that the market doesn't? → Brief panel (top 5 priority longs and shorts with the variant view) and the Variant view line in every thesis: the odds (or sales) today's price implies vs ours, and why we differ.
  3. What are the key catalysts and likely raises over 6 months, how do we take part, and what would we tell the CEO? → Brief panel (Major catalysts with positive and negative skew, likely raises, how we take part), What's next (every catalyst: how much it can move the stock, which way the risk skews, ★ written views), Capital (who owns each stock, specialist flows, issuance vs takeover cash) and the What I'd tell the CEO notes on every company card.

What I'd tell the CEO: the 4 Ms

CEOs are running the company; investors see the whole field, the tape and how holders price the stock. Every note fits one of four Ms:

MWhat investors see that the CEO may notExamples
MoneyWhen the window is open, how big a raise, who should anchor it, where to cut spendRaise after a run-up rather than into a binary readout; narrow spend to the lead when cash is short
MessageThe odds or sales the price implies vs the evidence, and the details and analyses investors are asking forDisclose the numbers and the target bar; dose-response and durability; launch metrics; date the catalysts
MovesPivots, acquisitions and in-licensing, partners, strategic review, positioning against the field leaderPivot a drug that failed in metastatic disease to the neoadjuvant setting where it worked; acquire a lower-risk, higher-reward asset to replace a failed lead; strategic review below cash
MilestonesThe path to approval and launch that the market will rewardBreakthrough designation and an early end-of-Phase 2 meeting; an FDA-agreed path after a miss; quarterly launch metrics

The questions a fund will ask (and where the answer lives)

#QuestionWhere the dashboard answers it todayWhat's still missing
1What's your edge?Fixed rubric across ~400 names: efficacy vs a numeric bar, one valuation formula, honest catalyst dates, frozen ledgers (Companies)—
2Show me your track record.Record page: frozen calls scored vs universe and XBI, what worked each quarter of 2025–26A portfolio, not just calls: sizing, daily P&L, Sharpe, hit rate, drawdown
3How do you size and manage risk?Inputs only: catalysts, PoS, runway, ours vs Street, catalyst impactPaper portfolio with sizing rules, XBI beta hedge, kill criteria
4Your top longs and shorts, and what's priced in?Brief panel; variant view (market-implied odds vs ours) in every thesisOptions-implied moves to check our event sizes
5How do you underwrite a binary event?What's next: impact (value riding on the event), skew (our odds vs typical, valuation, expectations, prior data), ★ written viewsScore each call after the event (did the skew call work?)
6Who raises in the next 90 days, and do we take part?Raise model (What's next, Brief), Capital › Liquidity (supply vs takeover cash), specialist flowsPast follow-on database (discount, warrants, size vs volume, 1/30/90-day returns, lead banks); shelf and ATM capacity
7How do you handle inside information from deals?Process answer onlyRestricted-list / wall-cross flags per company
8How much capital can this run?Daily volume per name; 13F ownership by type (specialists own ~30% of $300M–5B names)Short feasibility: short interest, borrow cost, days to cover; days to exit at 10–20% of volume
9What did you get wrong, and what did you change?Record page: valuation principles, Sep 12 backtest, frozen model changes; catalyst audit log in the runbook—
10What's your sector view?Areas drill-down; What worked next-quarter calls with a written backdropTakeover likelihood and deal comparables
11Can I trust the data?Frozen ledgers, logged input fixes with sources, monthly scheduled refresh, rerunnable repo, SEC 13F data—
12What would you tell management?What I'd tell the CEO notes (the 4 Ms) on every cardNotes written by hand for the priority names
13Who owns these stocks, and where is the crowding?Capital › Investors: ownership by type for every company (SEC 13F data set), 173 specialist funds' books, holding period, turnover, style, last quarter's buying and selling; holders on every cardCrowding score per name (specialist % × number of overlapping top funds) used in sizing
14How would you run the ECM book?Raise model + our participate / price-sensitive / pass view; net supply vs specialist capitalDeal participation record: deals we would have joined, allocation, pricing vs our value, returns after; which banks and which funds anchor which deals
15What's your portfolio's factor risk?—Factor exposures of the paper book: XBI beta, size, stage, cash-rich microcap, momentum; correlation clusters (many longs can be one bet)
16How do you compare with Baker, RA, Avoro?Capital leaderboard: 4Q/8Q copy-the-book returns, style vs peers, holding periodOur paper book shown on the same leaderboard
17What macro and policy risks matter?Next-quarter backdrop (rates, M&A, supply, policy)Policy tracker: FDA leadership and review behaviour, drug pricing (MFN/IRA), tariffs, China licensing share of deals
18How do you source ideas and run the team?Process answer; monthly refresh and runbook show the machineCoverage plan: who covers which areas, conference calendar, expert-network log

Build priority (in order)

  1. Paper portfolio from the frozen ledger: sizing (catalyst impact and skew, liquidity, crowding), beta hedge, daily P&L vs XBI, Sharpe, hit rate, drawdown; put it on the Capital leaderboard next to the specialist funds (answers 2, 3, 15, 16).
  2. Score every catalyst skew call after the event, and calibrate the rules (5).
  3. Follow-on deal database and deal participation record (6, 14).
  4. Short feasibility and crowding score (8, 13).
  5. Takeover-likelihood score and deal comparables (10).
  6. Policy tracker and China-licensing share (17).
  7. Compliance flags: restricted list and wall-cross log (7).

How to use this file

  • Every refresh: check the "What's still missing" column and move anything newly built into the middle column.
  • Every new request: say which question it helps answer.
  • Keep the honest version of question 2 current. The record is the first thing a fund will test.

Set Nov 24 2026. Update the table rather than the goals unless the goals themselves change.
